newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia, Estonia agree cross-border bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Latvia, Estonia agree cross-border bourse trade.

text.p: Latvia's central share depository said on Tuesday it had agreed with its Estonian counterpart that investors from both nations will be able to buy and sell on each other's bourses without formally registering in the country.

The new system will make share trading between the two states easier and a final agreement is expected by the middle of next year, Martinsh Rikshe, manager of the Latvian Share Depository, told a news conference.
"We have an oral agreement with the central share depository of Estonia to start preparations in January 1997 with the actual transaction procedures in place in July," Rikshe said.
Latvian and Estonian banks will also be able to keep the other country's securities in their accounts, which they are banned from doing at present.

Estonia currently has the most active share market in the Baltic states and it trades five times a week on a market-maker system. Its top stocks are all commercial banks but there is also a lively over-the-counter market.
Latvia uses a French-style order-driven system and trades on Tuesday/Wednesday and Thursday. Its most popular share is also a bank, Unibanka.
